title: Two bishops against a lone king
outcomes: Mates with two bishops and the king against a bare king from a position given, finding the quiet first move
Avoids the stalemate by counting the lone king's legal moves before a quiet move
Tells two bishops on opposite colours (can mate) from two on one colour (cannot)

steps.text: Two bishops on **opposite-coloured squares** can mate a lone king, but only with their own king close by. Your king takes away flight squares (squares the lone king could step to), the bishops attack squares of both colours near the corner, and a quiet bishop move (a waiting move) or a check forces the last steps. Watch one finish, then find the first move yourself.

steps.caption: White to move mates in three. Black's king is in the corner a8; White's king covers b7 and b8.

line.say: A quiet move. The bishop now covers a6, so after Ka7 and Bd4+ the king cannot step to a6.
The dark bishop checks along the diagonal to a7.
Black's king goes back to a8.
The light bishop checks on the long diagonal. Mate: the king covers b7 and b8, the other bishop a7.

claims.statement: Be2 starts a forced mate in three.
Black's king has the single legal move Ka7 after Be2, as it did before: Be2 does not take a flight square away.
After Be2 the bishop attacks a6.
Before Be2 the black king already has exactly one legal move.

steps.text: Three conditions. The bishops must stand on **opposite colours**: two bishops on one colour only draw. Your king must come close; bishops alone do not mate. And count Black's moves before any quiet move: if the king has no legal move and is not in check, the game is **stalemate**, a draw.

steps.title: Opposite colours or the same colour
steps.prompt: In the first position White wins. Now one bishop stands on a square of the other colour. Predict the result.

steps.title: The right check, or the stalemate
steps.prompt: In the first position Bb7+ mates in two. Now White plays the other bishop move instead. Is that checkmate, stalemate or neither?
Before each move or answer: did you count the lone king's legal moves, and did you check the colour of both bishops? Which did you forget?
